battle.name: 莫桑比克獨立戰爭
battle.brief: 莫桑比克獨立戰爭自1964年9月25日起爆發，葡屬殖民軍與莫桑比克民族解放陣線在前殖民地及內陸游擊區交戰，戰事延續至1974年。裝備方面，英國海軍於1862年服役的鐵甲艦（Ironclad）代表蒸汽鐵甲艦階段，並非本戰直接使用。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 鐵甲艦是英國皇家海軍十九世紀中葉重裝主力艦的類別，裝有蒸汽動力、鐵製防護與重型火炮，置於戰列艦編隊核心。

countries: 戰爭主場是當時由葡萄牙管治的莫桑比克，戰線並非單一前線，而是散在尼亞薩、卡布德爾加多、贊比亞與太特等省的山路、鐵路和行政城鎮周邊。葡萄牙控制洛倫索馬貴斯、貝拉與納卡拉等港口，再以納卡拉至楠普拉的運輸線、貝拉至太特鐵路和通往馬托拉的公路輸送部隊與補給。莫桑比克解放陣線於1962年2月在達爾薩拉姆成立後，把總部設在坦尚尼亞，利用當地的訓練場、營地與越境通道，並以贊比亞的盧薩卡作為後來談判地點。阿爾及利亞等北非方面也曾向解放陣線提供早期武器。因此，這是一場以莫桑比克為戰場、由葡萄牙維持殖民政權，並靠鄰國補給與外交支持維持運作的戰爭。
countriesEn: The principal theater was Portuguese Mozambique, where the fighting did not form a single front but ran through tracks, railways, and the approaches to administrative towns in Niassa, Cabo Delgado, Zambezia, and Tete. Portugal held the ports of Lourenço Marques, Beira, and Nacala, then moved troops and supplies through the Nacala-Nampula transport route, the Beira-Tete railway, and the road to Matola. After FRELIMO was founded in Dar es Salaam in February 1962, it based itself in Tanzania and used training facilities, camps, and border routes there, while Zambia later hosted the talks in Lusaka. Algeria and other North African channels also supplied FRELIMO with early weapons. The result was a war fought in Mozambique, sustained by Portugal's colonial state and by neighboring states' logistical and diplomatic support.
people: 莫桑比克解放陣線的主要領導人包括創黨兼首任主席愛杜華多·蒙德拉內、武裝部隊指揮薩莫拉·馬謝爾，以及負責軍隊組織與後續外交的若阿金·奇薩諾和馬塞利諾·多斯·桑托斯。蒙德拉內在1969年2月3日於達爾薩拉姆遇刺身亡，暗殺通常被判定與葡萄牙殖民安全體系的支持有關；他的死亡並未使解放陣線瓦解，馬謝爾接任黨內最高職務並加速游擊隊的整編。葡萄牙方面，一九六四年至一九六八年任莫桑比克總督的安東尼奧·德·斯皮諾拉主持大規模反游擊作戰，之後轉任國防部長；考爾·沙維爾·德·阿爾伯克魯克在一九六八年後接管前線指揮並出任總督。1974年葡萄牙政變後，斯皮諾拉在里斯本主張結束非洲戰事，奇薩諾與多斯·桑托斯則代表解放陣線參與盧薩卡談判。
peopleEn: The principal FRELIMO leaders included founder and first president Eduardo Mondlane, armed-forces commander Samora Machel, and Joaquim Chissano and Marcelino dos Santos, who handled military organization and later diplomacy. Mondlane was assassinated in Dar es Salaam on 3 February 1969, an act generally judged to have involved support from the Portuguese colonial security apparatus; his death did not break the movement, and Machel assumed the movement's highest office and accelerated the reorganization of its guerrilla forces. On the Portuguese side, António de Spínola, governor-general of Mozambique from 1964 to 1968, directed major counterinsurgency campaigns before becoming defense minister. Kaul Xavier de Albuquerque took command in the field after 1968 and subsequently served as governor-general. Following Portugal's 1974 revolution, Spínola advocated ending the African wars in Lisbon, while Chissano and dos Santos represented FRELIMO in the Lusaka negotiations.
kits: 葡萄牙步兵廣泛使用比利時FN FAL與德國Heckler & Koch G3突擊步槍，兩者同樣發射7.62×51毫米北約彈；連級支援火力包括FN MAG重機槍，部分部隊仍配備Browning M1919輕機槍。軍官與護衛使用Browning Hi-Power手槍，Sterling及Uzi則用於近衛、車隊與狹小空間的防衛。英制二英吋迫擊炮及三英吋、亦即81公釐級迫擊炮，負責曲射支援。Fiat G.91、T-6 Texan、Alouette II或III直升機及P-2V Neptune分別承擔對地攻擊、觀察 liaison、運輸與沿海巡邏任務。解放陣線初期的武器主要為Lee-Enfield步槍、手槍、輕機槍及少量繳獲品，外援增加後則取得AK-47、SKS步槍、RPG-2火箭筒、RPD輕機槍與82公釐迫擊炮。7.62×39毫米與7.62×51毫米彈藥不能互換，不同長度的彈匣、槍托和備件也難以通用，使兩套供應系統的後勤負擔格外沉重。
kitsEn: Portuguese infantry widely used the Belgian FN FAL and German Heckler & Koch G3 assault rifles, both firing 7.62×51mm NATO ammunition. Company-level support included the FN MAG machine gun, while some formations retained Browning M1919 light machine guns. Officers and guards carried Browning Hi-Power pistols, while Sterling and Uzi submachine guns were used for close protection, vehicle crews, and confined spaces. British two-inch mortars and three-inch, or 81mm-class, mortars provided curved fire support. Fiat G.91s, T-6 Texans, Alouette II or III helicopters, and P-2V Neptunes performed ground attack, liaison observation, transport, and coastal patrol duties. FRELIMO initially relied on Lee-Enfield rifles, pistols, light machine guns, and a limited quantity of captured weapons; later aid brought AK-47 and SKS rifles, RPG-2 rocket launchers, RPD light machine guns, and 82mm mortars. Because 7.62×39mm and 7.62×51mm ammunition were not interchangeable and magazines, stocks, and spare parts differed, the two supply systems created a substantial logistics burden.
tactics: 1964年至1966年間，解放陣線採取游擊戰而非據城作戰。小型突擊隊多在夜間移動，接近孤立葡軍哨所或車隊後短時間射擊，再迅速退回森林；同時破壞鐵軌、橋梁與通訊設施，並利用雨季道路泥濘和乾季能見度改變突擊條件。葡軍則以守備據點、營級或數營組成的臨時支隊、空中偵察、直升機快速反應、迫擊炮及G.91空襲協同追掃。1966年末至1967年前後的「海鷗行動」雖迫使部分解放陣線隊伍分散，葡軍卻屢次只找到已撤空的營地，未能摧毀其指揮核心。1968年後，解放陣線在尼亞薩及贊比亞一帶建立較固定的基地，組成步兵連、營、迫擊炮組、通訊與後勤單位，開始進行持續數日、協調多支小隊的攻擊，並把火力集中於葡軍哨站、運輸線和補給點。葡萄牙隨後以護送縱隊、封鎖道路和鞏固主要交通軸線應對，但車隊在 ambush 下仍容易遭受局部伏擊。
tacticsEn: From 1964 to 1966, FRELIMO fought as a guerrilla force rather than attempting to occupy towns. Small strike teams usually moved at night, closed on isolated Portuguese posts or convoys, fired for a short period, and withdrew into the forest. They also cut rails, damaged bridges and communications facilities, and adapted their timing to muddy rainy-season roads and changes in dry-season visibility. Portugal responded with garrison posts, temporary task forces built around one or more battalions, aerial reconnaissance, helicopter-borne reaction forces, mortar fire, and G.91 air attacks. Operation Seagull around late 1966 and 1967 forced some FRELIMO groups to disperse, but Portuguese columns repeatedly found evacuated camps and failed to destroy the movement's command structure. After 1968, FRELIMO established more permanent bases in Niassa and Zambezia, organized infantry companies, battalions, mortar teams, signals, and logistics units, and began coordinated operations lasting several days. These attacks concentrated on Portuguese posts, transport links, and supply points. Portugal then relied on protected convoys, road interdiction, and fortified transport corridors, although convoys remained vulnerable to localized ambushes.
data: 可核對的時間節點顯示，這場戰爭不是從全面進攻開始。1964年9月25日，解放陣線在尼亞薩省攻擊葡方警察與軍事哨所，開啟公開武裝衝突；當時參戰者仍以流動的小型突擊單位為主。葡方以固定守備、巡邏連、分遣支隊及航空兵力構成防線，解放陣線則在1965年至1967年間逐步增加營地、武器和訓練。1966年末至1967年的「海鷗行動」是葡軍一次重要追掃，結果是找到撤退後的營地，而非取得決定性全勝。1968年解放陣線完成較大規模的軍事編組，基層由小分隊改為連與營，並增設迫擊炮、工兵、通信和後勤組。1969年2月3日蒙德拉內遇刺；1970年6月25日葡萄牙單方面宣告莫桑比克獨立，但解放陣線拒絕該安排，戰鬥繼續。1974年9月7日簽訂盧薩卡協議，1975年6月25日完成獨立與政權交接。解放陣線的早期補給由達爾薩拉姆經公路送至邊境，再以車輛、畜力及人力背運送往前線營地；葡軍則由港口經鐵路與公路運至區域倉庫，以空運維持偏遠哨站。現存葡方與解放陣線記錄多為零散戰報，總傷亡數字互相衝突，因此無法可靠列出精確總數。
dataEn: The documented chronology shows that the war did not begin with a general offensive. On 25 September 1964, FRELIMO attacked a Portuguese police and military post in Niassa Province, opening the armed conflict, while the participants were still organized mainly as mobile small strike units. Portugal built its defense around fixed garrisons, patrol companies, detached task forces, and aviation; between 1965 and 1967, FRELIMO gradually expanded its camps, weapons, and training. Operation Seagull in late 1966 and 1967 was an important Portuguese sweep, but it found evacuated camps rather than achieving a decisive victory. In 1968 FRELIMO completed a larger military reorganization, changing small detachments into companies and battalions and adding mortar, engineer, signals, and logistics sections. Mondlane was assassinated on 3 February 1969. Portugal unilaterally declared Mozambique independent on 25 June 1970, but FRELIMO rejected the arrangement and the fighting continued. The Lusaka Accord followed on 7 September 1974, and independence and the transfer of authority were completed on 25 June 1975. Early FRELIMO supplies moved by road from Dar es Salaam to the border and were then carried by vehicle, animal transport, and human porters to forward camps. Portugal moved cargo from the ports by rail and road to regional depots, using airlift for isolated posts. Surviving Portuguese and FRELIMO records consist largely of fragmented reports and conflicting total casualty figures, so no precise overall casualty total can be treated as reliable.
cause: 直接背景是葡萄牙拒絕在可預見期限內把主權交給莫桑比克的政治團體。卡邦薩政府雖承認某些內部自治改革，仍以總督、駐軍、警察與情報機關維持直接統治，談判未能產生獨立時間表。莫桑比克解放陣線由MANU與UDENAMO於1962年合併而成，原本希望在達爾薩拉姆以宣言、陳情和聯合會議擴大政治壓力；當這些方式無法迫使里斯本改變政策，組織才把武裝鬥爭列為主要手段。坦尚尼亞提供的營地、訓練與越境通道，使解放陣線能保存幹部和持續接應武器，而莫桑比克內陸的道路、森林與分散葡軍哨位，又使早期小隊可利用葡萄牙情報和長距離補給的弱點。1964年的首度進擊因此兼具試探與奪取武器的目的：既要證明分散游擊能迫使葡軍分兵，也要為建立游擊控制區取得裝備和活動空間。
causeEn: The immediate background was Portugal's refusal to transfer sovereignty to Mozambican political organizations within a foreseeable timetable. Although the Caetanos government acknowledged some forms of internal autonomy, it preserved direct rule through governors, garrisons, police, and intelligence services, and negotiations produced no date for independence. FRELIMO emerged from the merger of MANU and UDENAMO in 1962 and initially intended to expand political pressure through declarations, petitions, and joint meetings from Dar es Salaam. When those methods failed to force a change in Lisbon, the organization made armed struggle its principal means. Camps, training, and border routes in Tanzania allowed FRELIMO to preserve its leadership and receive weapons, while Mozambique's interior roads, forests, and dispersed Portuguese posts gave small teams opportunities to exploit weaknesses in Portuguese intelligence and long-range supply. The first incursions in 1964 therefore served both as tests and as means of acquiring arms, while establishing the zones from which guerrilla activity could expand.
impact: 葡萄牙的反游擊行動在局部戰鬥中造成解放陣線損失，也能依賴空軍、迫擊炮與裝甲車迅速打擊暴露的突擊隊，但始終無法同時消滅多個根據地、取得領導人並切斷全部跨境補給。這種戰術上有效而戰略上難以收束的局面，迫使葡軍長期依賴納卡拉至楠普拉、貝拉至太特及洛倫索馬貴斯周邊的運輸線。解放陣線則發生根本轉變：早期只靠小隊、獵槍和突擊的組織，到1968年後已能維持營地，運用連、營、迫擊炮、通信和後勤單位，並在1973年至1974年間把營級攻擊投向貝拉至太特及納卡拉至楠普拉沿線，使葡軍不得不持續防衛道路、城鎮與補給節點。這種軍事存續能力改變了談判地位，促使里斯本在1974年承認解放陣線有權決定莫桑比克政治前途。獨立後，解放陣線也把戰時建立的軍隊、指揮系統和後勤組織轉入國家政權，成為新政府的核心軍事資產。
impactEn: Portuguese counterinsurgency operations inflicted losses on individual FRELIMO groups and could use aircraft, mortars, and armored vehicles against exposed strike teams, but they could not simultaneously destroy every base, capture the leadership, and sever all cross-border supply. This pattern of tactical effectiveness without strategic closure obliged Portugal to rely continuously on the Nacala-Nampula, Beira-Tete, and Lourenço Marques transport corridors. FRELIMO underwent a fundamental transformation: an organization initially equipped with small teams, hunting rifles, and raids developed permanent camps and the capacity to employ companies, battalions, mortars, signals, and logistics units. Between 1973 and 1974, battalion-sized attacks along the Beira-Tete and Nacala-Nampula axes forced Portugal to defend roads, towns, and supply nodes continuously. This operational survival changed the diplomatic balance and led Lisbon in 1974 to recognize FRELIMO's right to determine Mozambique's political future. At independence, FRELIMO transferred the army, command system, and logistics organization built during the war into the new state, where they became central military assets.
result: 1970年6月25日葡萄牙宣布殖民地獨立，只改變了法律名稱，沒有改變莫桑比克大部分地區仍由葡軍與殖民行政控制的事實；解放陣線拒絕承認，戰爭因而再延續四年。1974年4月25日葡萄牙革命後里斯本改變非洲政策，9月7日在盧薩卡簽訂協議。協議的主要內容包括葡萄牙承認解放陣線決定莫桑比克政治前途的權利、停止敵對行動、縮減並分階段撤離葡軍，以及成立過渡權力機構。1975年6月舉行選舉後，解放陣線取得組政府的多數位置；6月25日莫桑比克正式獨立，薩莫拉·馬謝爾出任總理並兼任國防部長。葡萄牙對解放陣線的殖民戰鬥角色至此在協議與獨立安排下終止，駐軍依後續安排陸續離開；此後在莫桑比克發生的內部武裝衝突屬於另一階段，不應倒算為這場反殖民戰爭的延長。
resultEn: Portugal's declaration of independence on 25 June 1970 changed the legal name of the colony but not the fact that Portuguese troops and colonial officials still controlled most of Mozambique. FRELIMO refused to recognize it, and the war continued for another four years. After Portugal's revolution on 25 April 1974, Lisbon reversed its African policy, and the Lusaka Accord was signed on 7 September. Its principal terms recognized FRELIMO's right to determine Mozambique's political future, required a halt to hostilities and a phased reduction and withdrawal of Portuguese troops, and provided for an interim authority. After the elections of June 1975, FRELIMO secured the positions needed to form the government. Mozambique became independent on 25 June, with Samora Machel serving as prime minister and defense minister. The colonial combat role of Portuguese forces against FRELIMO ended under the accord and independence arrangements, with troop withdrawals continuing under subsequent schedules. The internal armed conflict that followed in Mozambique belonged to a separate phase and should not be retroactively treated as a continuation of this anti-colonial war.
